content:
The Guardian reports that Apple is in talks with several companies over acquiring the US broadcast rights to The Open Championship. Netflix and Amazon are also expected to show interest in those broadcast rights.

Founded in Scotland in 1860, The Open Championship is the oldest of the four men's major golf tournaments, organised by the R&A. It is commonly referred to in the United States as 'The British Open' to distinguish it from another major tournament, the US Open.

NBC secured the rights to broadcast The Open Championship in 2017, signing a 12-year deal that saw them beat out ESPN. The broadcast rights are held jointly by NBC and Versant, which operates the Golf Channel. The R&A has said it expects to enter into discussions with NBC, Versant and other interested parties regarding the rights.

The latest report states that Apple has begun 'preliminary talks' with the R&A over bidding for The Open Championship. The report cites a 'person familiar with the matter' and notes that Apple 'remains committed to investing in sports broadcasting rights and will continue to look for suitable sports assets'.

An R&A spokesperson, responding to a query from The Guardian, said:

'Our partnership with NBC and Versant has been excellent, delivering outstanding results for The Open, the AIG Women's Open, and our other championships and international events. Looking ahead to the next cycle of R&A media rights in the United States, we expect to engage with our existing partners NBC and Versant in due course, while continuing to monitor developments in the broadcast industry and the level of interest in our rights from various parties.'

Apple last year announced it had become the exclusive US broadcast partner for Formula 1 (F1). The company also broadcasts Friday Night Baseball, Major League Baseball's Friday night games, as well as Major League Soccer (MLS) matches.
